title: Customer Ambit: Quickprobes and Request Docket
content:
Purpose and headline

Short: this is a compact working synthesis of customer requests observed between 2025-10 and 2025-11 across support, CSM calls, and product trials. Aim is to propose 6 low-risk quick-probes (2–6 engineering days) and 2 scoped platform experiments that materially reduce support load or clarify cost/latency tradeoffs. This is intentionally pragmatic: we prioritize fixes that unblock customers or reduce Ops overhead.

Observed signal clusters (high-level)

1) Predictable tail latency anomalies when KV cache is warm but throughput spikes (15 customers, median repro in staging).
2) Confusing model selection behavior for multi-variant routing — customers expect explicit fallback logs (7 accounts requested visibility).
3) Prompt/stream truncation with streaming + function-calls in mobile SDKs (4 customers experiencing partial outputs).
4) Cost/quality questions around quantized private deployments — customers ask for sample-regression reports and a simple toggle in Console (10 asks).

Representative vignettes

- Retail Search (Customer A): nightly batch peak causes a subset of requests to fall back to slower model variants; client perceives this as degraded relevance and escalated to CSM. They asked for: a) per-request rationale for fallback, b) ability to pin route to a specific variant during sale windows.

- Health SaaS (Customer B): on private Dedicated deployment, after a minor kernel update some long-context chat sessions start dropping final function-call payloads when streaming. They attribute to streaming framing differences and want a reliable failover method that preserves last token.

- Marketplace (Customer C): concerned about tokens-per-embedding cost when switching to int8 quantization in a staging run; wants automated quality delta report (10k samples) and cost delta estimate before enabling across prod.

Quick-probes (low cost, quick signals)

QP-1: Tail-latency sampler + repro harness (3 eng days)
- What: lightweight load harness to reproduce warm-cache spike and capture kernel selection + per-request route logs.
- Why: confirms whether fallback policy misfires under bursty traffic.
- Output: reproducible test + annotated trace template for CS to attach to escalations.
- Owner: Jonah Lee; Due: 2025-12-15.

QP-2: Fallback-explain flag in logs (4 eng days)
- What: add per-request fallback_reason field to debug logs (Console-visible or via trace export).
- Why: gives customers the visibility they keep asking for without full UI changes.
- Output: log spec + sample dashboard query saved.
- Owner: Miguel Santos; Due: 2026-01-05.

QP-3: Streaming frame resiliency test (4 eng days)
- What: test harness that sends function-calling streams with deliberate frame loss and checks reconnection/final-payload delivery.
- Why: validate and reproduce reported truncation.
- Output: test cases + recommended SDK patch.
- Owner: Priya Kapoor; Due: 2025-12-22.

QP-4: Console micro-report for quantization trial (5 eng days + 2 UX days)
- What: a small Console widget to run a sample-quality-vs-cost preview for selected model/quant profile on 1k sample prompts.
- Why: reduces friction for customers hesitant to flip quantization in private deployments.
- Output: mock + working backend job + docs.
- Owner: Aisha Nadar (product lead) + UX; Due: 2026-01-20.

QP-5: Mobile SDK streaming quick-fix patch (2 eng days)
- What: guard to ensure final function-call payload is buffered and re-emitted on reconnect for iOS/Android SDKs.
- Why: immediate ops-reducer for mobile customers.
- Output: patch + release notes.
- Owner: Mobile SDK owner (TBD); Due: 2025-12-18.

QP-6: Customer-facing short playbook (1 day CS + 1 day eng)
- What: one-pager for CSMs detailing diagnostics steps for tail-latency and fallback incidents (what to collect before escalation).
- Why: reduces time-to-triangle and unnecessary escalations.
- Output: playbook doc and sample collection script.
- Owner: CS ops; Due: 2025-12-10.

Scoped experiments (medium cost, higher impact)

SE-1: Route explainability + canned rollouts (3 weeks)
- Scope: build (a) route-explain API surface that returns the policy decision tree used for a request and (b) a lightweight Console view for pinning/forcing variants per-route for a window.
- Why: addresses multiple asks about visibility and manual control during promotions. Helps sales/CS win confidence.
- Success metric: reduction in manual escalations for route surprises by 60% within 6 weeks.
- Owner: product + runtime; Target start: 2026-01-25.

SE-2: Quantization trial harness and regression report pipeline (4 weeks)
- Scope: offline harness to run N=10k sample prompts across model/quant combos, compute QA deltas (embedding cosine, generation ROUGE/BERTScore subsets), and produce a one-click report.
- Why: large enterprise customers ask for deterministic guardrails before flipping quantized models in Dedicated/Private.
- Success metric: 80% fewer 'rollback' requests for post-quantization regressions in first 90 days.
- Owner: applied-ml + product-optimize; Target start: 2026-02-01.

Uncertainties and constraints

- Data access: some Private customers cannot share 10k prompts; we'll need synthetic proxies or permissioned sample flows. This increases SE-2 scope if manual permission flows required.
- SLA considerations: adding verbose fallback logs may increase trace storage costs; need cost estimate and sample retention policy.
- Cross-team bandwidth: runtime kernel team has a planned maintenance window mid-Jan; time QP-1 and SE-1 accordingly.

Immediate asks for review (what I want from this doc)

1) Product: approve QP-4 scope and prioritize UX time (2 days).
2) Runtime: confirm whether QP-1 is feasible in 3 days or needs more.
3) CS: agree to pilot the playbook with 3 chosen CSMs and provide sample escalations by 2025-12-08.

Quick cost/effort heuristics (rough)

- QP items: 2–5 eng days each, total ~20 eng days + 2 UX days.
- SE items: 3–4 weeks each, cross-functional, estimated ~8–12 eng-weeks combined including QA and docs.

Next steps and owners (short-run)

- 2025-12-04: sync meeting (CS/Product/Runtime) to align on priorities; owner: Aisha Nadar.
- 2025-12-05: Jonah to drop initial harness PR for QP-1 into repo with README.
- 2025-12-08: CS to deliver 3 pilot cases and sample escalation artifacts.
- 2025-12-10: CS ops publishes playbook draft for review.

Notes to self / open questions

- Do we prefer to expose fallback_reason as a structured field or a free-text explanation? Structured is better for dashboards but requires enumeration.
- How do we communicate extra trace storage costs to customers cleanly in Console? Could be opt-in by default for enterprise tiers only.
- For SE-2, what minimal sampling size gives meaningful QA signal? (Priya to propose stats threshold.)

Relevant links and threads

- Slack: #cs-runtime-ops thread dated 2025-11-18 (see pinned messages).
- Support ticket examples: TKT-98321, TKT-98909 (attached in internal ticket binder).
- Confluence draft: 'Ambit notes 2025-11' (linked above).

Footer / versioning

This is v0.1 working draft — expect edits after the 2025-12-04 sync. If you have urgent asks to add to quick-probes, drop them in the meeting agenda or ping me directly (Aisha).
